resolutions.researcher_notes: Searched hard, found nothing that states a 1953 start/construction year for this system. Ruled out: the seed A Barrel Full link (banned source, not opened). OGJ's 2023 expansion article (Tejas/Howard Energy Eagle Ford system expansion) covers only the 2023 project, no founding history. Kinder Morgan's Natural-Gas/Index page describes the current ~3,800-mile Tejas intrastate system (Texas Gulf Coast) but gives no start year. Bloomberg private-company snapshot URL now 301-redirects/dead. Checked SEC EDGAR full-text search (efts.sec.gov, covers 2001-present) for '"Tejas Gas" 1953' (0 hits) and '"Tejas Gas Corporation"' (38 hits, all later-era proxy-statement bios of executives who once worked there, none describing pipeline founding). Checked Texas State Historical Association Handbook of Texas (no standalone entry found; search redirected in a loop). Checked Wikipedia (no article for Tejas Gas Corporation). Search-engine access is degraded this session (WebSearch quota exhausted; Google and Bing both return JS-gated/empty result shells to a plain fetch), so a targeted phrase search for '1953' could not be run through a real search index. No source found to support or contradict StartYear1=1953 -- reporting UNRESOLVED, not a refutation.

No source found stating a 120 MMcf/d capacity for this specific segment/system. Kinder Morgan's current Tejas system description (kindermorgan.com/Operations/Natural-Gas/Index) gives no per-system or per-segment capacity figure, only total mileage (~3,800 mi) for the whole intrastate network (which now also includes acquired South Shore, Mission Valley, La Salle and Red Gate pipelines, so even if a capacity figure existed there it would not isolate this original Refugio-to-Fort Bend segment). The 2023 OGJ article's 2 Bcf/d figure is for the NEW Freer-to-Sinton expansion line, not this segment, and is not usable to corroborate 120 MMcf/d. Reuters (2017 Refugio pipeline fire, via Wayback) does not give a capacity figure either. No RRC/FERC capacity record located (Tejas is intrastate, so it is not FERC-jurisdictional -- FERC eLibrary was not checked further per the brief's warning that FERC silence is not informative here). UNRESOLVED.

No source found stating a 5,221 km length for this segment. CONCERN (not a value change -- flagging only): 5,221 km (~3,245 mi) is implausible as the point-to-point length of a Refugio County-to-Fort Bend County, TX segment (straight-line distance is roughly 240 km / 150 mi), but it lands close in order of magnitude to Kinder Morgan's own description of the CURRENT Tejas intrastate system as '~3,800 miles of pipeline ... primarily along the Texas Gulf Coast' (kindermorgan.com/Operations/Natural-Gas/Index, fetched live) -- i.e. this reads like a network-wide mileage figure attached to a single named segment/row, the same aggregate-vs-segment pattern flagged elsewhere in this project (e.g. Kazakhstan gas, Egypt P4788). Not close enough to the KM figure (3,245 mi vs ~3,800 mi, and KM's figure includes several pipelines Tejas acquired after this row's era) to cite as a match, so no ref is proposed and the unit stays UNRESOLVED -- but Update should look at whether this LengthKnown value belongs to the whole Tejas/Kinder Morgan Texas intrastate grid rather than one segment.

Reuters, 'Kinder Morgan gas pipeline explodes in Texas, no injuries' (Feb 15, 2017): reports a fire/explosion 'on its Tejas pipeline in a rural area of Refugio, Texas, about 45 miles north of Corpus Christi' -- directly names Refugio, Texas as a location the Tejas pipeline runs through, supporting the sheet's StartLocation='Refugio County'. Live reuters.com returns HTTP 401 to a plain fetch (bot-wall, confirmed by direct curl -- not a deletion), so the Wayback capture (2022-02-24, verifier PASS on 'Refugio'+'Tejas') is proposed in its place per the blocked-origin rule. Only the Refugio (start) end is corroborated by this source; no independent source located for the Fort Bend County end -- checked SEC EDGAR full-text search ('"Tejas Pipeline" "Fort Bend"', 6 hits), but the one substantive hit (Energy Transfer Partners 2009 10-Q Exhibit 10.2, a sprawling multi-entity Kinder Morgan/Houston Pipe Line Co. asset-and-bond schedule) mentions 'Fort Bend' only in an unrelated Houston Pipe Line Company right-of-way bond entry, not tied to the Tejas Refugio segment specifically -- too ambiguous to cite without risking a false attribution, so it was not used. Tier kept at medium/single-source since only one end of the route is corroborated and by one publisher.
